governance.sharingPolicy: presented to the employer, the works council and the health and safety committee; submitted to the labour inspectorate and regional authorities; contains only aggregated data; never shared between tenants

assets.name: Collective Health Indicator
assets.description: Anonymised population-level health and exposure indicators built under the physician's responsibility: prevalence of abnormal audiometry, spirometry or vision results per exposure group, psychosocial risk questionnaire scores per unit, fitness restriction patterns per workstation, vaccination coverage, sentinel events and epidemiological alerts, exposure and health cross-tabulations for the prevention plan, with the aggregation rules, minimum group-size thresholds, cohort definitions and the physician's release decision. Produced by Collective Health Monitoring (cohm) from medical data and exposure profiles and shared with prevention as collective advice.
assets.businessMeaning: The physician's third job, turning individual findings into collective prevention, expressed as data that can leave the medical perimeter because no individual can be recognised in it.
assets.accessScope: occupational physicians define and release; the service manager, HSE manager and the health and safety committee read released indicators; alerts below threshold visible to physicians only; Kitry data specialists support cohort definition without seeing individual data

interfaces.name: collective-health api
interfaces.description: Cohort definition, aggregation rule, threshold check, indicator computation, physician release and alert API used by collective health monitoring, dashboards, the annual report and risk assessment.

interfaces.name: collective health events
interfaces.description: Indicator computed, threshold alert raised, released and withdrawn events consumed by risk assessment, dashboards, the annual report and the audit trail.

governance.retention: released indicators kept indefinitely as anonymised data; cohort definitions and release decisions kept 10 years; indicators below the minimum group size never persisted outside the medical perimeter
governance.sharingPolicy: released indicators shared with the employer, the works council and the health and safety committee as collective prevention advice; anonymised sector benchmarks shared across tenants only with customer consent; underlying individual data never leaves the medical perimeter

rootGroups.name: Platform and Services
rootGroups.description: The foundation and the service arm: accounts and roles with medical segregation, tenant configuration for shared and dedicated HDS SaaS, the immutable audit trail required by HDS and ISO 27001, the FR/BE/LU/NL regulation content Kitry maintains, ecosystem integration connections, and the implementation projects and support tickets through which Kitry's consultants deploy, migrate, train and support every customer.

subGroups.name: Identity, Configuration and Audit
subGroups.description: User accounts and roles, tenant configuration, audit trail entries and the country regulation rules that parameterise the platform.

assets.name: User Account and Role
assets.description: Every account on the platform and what it may do: occupational physicians, nurses, medical assistants, service coordinators, HSE managers and prevention advisers, HR administrators, managers, employees, works council guest readers, external auditors and Kitry staff, with the tenant, the role profiles configured per customer, medical and non-medical role separation, site and unit scopes, SSO federation with the customer's identity provider (SAML, OpenID Connect), MFA enrolment, professional registration numbers for physicians, sessions, invitations, delegations and deactivation. Managed by Identity, SSO, Roles and Consent (iden) and the basis of every authorisation decision, including the medical segregation enforced with Consent and Access Grant.
assets.businessMeaning: The gate that makes one platform safe for physicians, HR, managers and 6,000+ active users at once; a role misconfiguration is the fastest route to a medical secrecy breach.
assets.accessScope: tenant security administrators for their own users and roles; the service manager for medical role assignments; the user for their own profile; Kitry platform operations for support and tenant provisioning under logged access

interfaces.name: identity api
interfaces.description: Authentication, SSO federation, MFA, role profile, scope, delegation, session and deactivation API used by every module, the portals, the confidentiality controls and the audit trail.

interfaces.name: account events
interfaces.description: Created, role changed, scope changed, SSO federated, MFA enrolled, logged in, delegation started, deactivated and locked events consumed by confidentiality enforcement, notifications, portals and the audit trail.

governance.retention: accounts kept for the life of the user plus 3 years after deactivation for audit; login and session logs 12 months; role change history kept 10 years
governance.sharingPolicy: internal to the tenant; identity attributes exchanged with the customer's identity provider under SSO; never shared between tenants

assets.name: Tenant Configuration
assets.description: The configured shape of one customer's platform: enabled modules and hosting tier (shared or dedicated HDS SaaS), languages (FR, NL, EN), countries and establishments in scope, sector pre-configuration applied, configured forms and fields for consultations, questionnaires, risk assessment and accident capture, workflows and business rules, role profiles, document templates and corporate identity, notification templates and channels, surveillance rule overrides within the country content, numbering schemes, integration parameters and release-train status, with versions, change requests and the consultant who applied them. Managed by the Configuration Engine (cfgr), operated on the hosting tier by HDS/ISO 27001 Hosting and Tenant Isolation (host), built during implementation and changed by support.
assets.businessMeaning: Configurable to each customer's needs without code is the promise of Kitry as a Service; the configuration object is the product each implementation consultant actually delivers.
assets.accessScope: tenant administrators of the customer for their own configuration; Kitry implementation, support and platform staff under change control; medical form configuration reviewed by the chief physician; never visible across tenants

interfaces.name: tenant-configuration api
interfaces.description: Module, hosting tier, language, form, workflow, rule, role profile, template and integration parameter configuration API with versioning and change requests used by the configuration engine, hosting operations, implementation, support and every module at runtime.

interfaces.name: configuration packages
interfaces.description: Exportable configuration packages and sector pre-configurations moved between test and production tenants and reused across implementations.

interfaces.name: configuration events
interfaces.description: Module enabled, form changed, workflow changed, rule overridden, template published, hosting tier changed and release applied events consumed by every module, implementation project tracking, support and the audit trail.

governance.retention: versions kept for the life of the tenant and 5 years after contract end; configuration in effect at any date reconstructible for audit
governance.sharingPolicy: internal to the customer and Kitry; sector pre-configurations shared across tenants as Kitry intellectual property without customer data; never customer-specific content across tenants

assets.name: Audit Trail Entry
assets.description: An immutable record of an auditable action: who (account, role, tenant, session, IP range), what (read, create, update, sign, release, export, download, transfer, break-glass, configuration change, role change, declaration submission), on which object (with special tagging for every access to health data in the medical schema), when, from which module and integration, with before and after references for changes, justification for break-glass, and the retention class applied. Written by every brick through Audit Trail and Data Retention (audt), stored in the append-only audit log, required by HDS certification, ISO 27001 and the medical secrecy accountability of the customer's physicians, and used to answer worker access requests and security investigations.
assets.businessMeaning: The evidence that medical secrecy and tenant isolation actually hold; the first thing a data protection officer, an HDS auditor or a physician asks for when access is questioned.
assets.accessScope: tenant security administrators and the data protection officer for their tenant; the chief physician for accesses to the medical schema; Kitry security and platform operations for cross-tenant security monitoring; HDS and ISO 27001 auditors; never editable by anyone

interfaces.name: audit-trail api
interfaces.description: Append, query by actor, object, period and category, medical-access report, worker access-request report and retention execution API used by every module, confidentiality monitoring, hosting operations, the data protection officer's tooling and auditors.

interfaces.name: audit extracts
interfaces.description: Signed audit extracts for HDS and ISO 27001 audits, customer security reviews and worker access requests.

interfaces.name: audit events
interfaces.description: Entry appended, medical access detected outside grant, break-glass opened, export performed and retention executed events consumed by confidentiality monitoring, security alerting and hosting operations.

governance.retention: entries kept at least 10 years and, for accesses to health data, for the retention period of the medical file concerned so that any access can be explained over the file's life; immutable, tamper-evident, replicated per tenant
governance.sharingPolicy: internal to the tenant and Kitry's security function; extracts provided to HDS and ISO 27001 auditors, the customer's data protection officer and the worker for their own file; never shared between tenants

assets.name: Country Regulation Rule
assets.description: The regulatory content Kitry maintains for France, Belgium, Luxembourg and the Netherlands: examination types and surveillance categories, periodicities and their triggers per exposure and worker attribute, professionals authorised per act, fitness opinion forms and wording, medical file retention rules (French DMST decree 2022-1434, Belgian Code on well-being at work), DUERP and prevention plan requirements, accident and disease declaration deadlines, forms and connectors, occupational disease tables, annual report templates and the effective dates, legal references, change notes and versions of each rule, with the sector and customer overrides allowed. Maintained in Country Regulation Content (regc) by occupational health lawyers and content specialists, consumed by the surveillance engine, declarations, reports and the configuration engine, and released with the regulatory release train.
assets.businessMeaning: Thirty-five years of regulatory know-how encoded as rules; keeping every customer current with FR/BE/LU/NL change without disruption is the implementation team's promise and this content is how it is kept.
assets.accessScope: Kitry regulatory content specialists edit and release; implementation and support consultants read; customers' physicians, HSE and HR read the rules applicable to them with legal references; customers may override only where the rule allows

interfaces.name: regulation-content api
interfaces.description: Effective-dated rule query per country, examination type, exposure and worker attribute, form and deadline lookup, rule simulation and release management API used by the surveillance engine, declarations, reports, the configuration engine and the content back office.

interfaces.name: regulatory release notes
interfaces.description: Release notes and legal reference packs published to customers with every regulatory release.

interfaces.name: regulation content events
interfaces.description: Rule published, rule superseded, form version changed and release applied events consumed by the surveillance engine (recomputation), declarations, configuration and support notifications.

governance.retention: effective-dated versions kept permanently so that the rule in force at any past date can be reproduced for a file, a declaration or a report
governance.sharingPolicy: Kitry intellectual property shared with all customers as product content; legal references public; never contains customer data

subGroups.name: Integrations and Services
subGroups.description: Integration connections to HRIS, SSO, e-signature, telehealth, SMS, devices and national bodies, and the implementation projects and support tickets of Kitry's service teams.

assets.name: Integration Connection
assets.description: A configured link between the platform and an external system for one tenant: HRIS connectors (SAP SuccessFactors, Workday, ADP, national public-sector HR systems, file-based feeds), SSO identity providers, the Goodflag electronic signature service, the Vonage telehealth service, the Cegedim SMS gateway, connected measurement devices (Eolys, FIM, Essilor, JLM Medical, Siemens) and their drivers, national reporting connectors (Ameli and net-entreprises, Belgian Portal of Social Security, insurers, Fedris) and outbound webhooks, with endpoint, protocol, field mappings, schedule, credentials referenced by vault id, health status, error log and volume statistics. Managed by Ecosystem Integrations (intg) and HRIS Synchronisation and Import (hris) and set up during implementation.
assets.businessMeaning: The plumbing that makes the platform the hub of the customer's HR, medical device and public-body ecosystem; its health decides whether data flows without an IT project on the customer side.
assets.accessScope: Kitry integration engineers and implementation consultants; tenant integration administrators for their own connections; credentials never readable, referenced by vault id; connection health visible in support

interfaces.name: integration-connection api
interfaces.description: Connection setup, mapping, schedule, credential reference, test, health, error log and volume API used by the integration hub, HRIS import, device capture, e-signature, telehealth, SMS, national connectors, implementation and support.

interfaces.name: integration health events
interfaces.description: Connection created, run succeeded, run failed, credential expiring, mapping changed and disabled events consumed by support alerting, implementation project tracking, dashboards and the audit trail.

governance.retention: connection definitions kept for the life of the connection plus 3 years; error and run logs kept 3 years; payloads in the staging zone purged on the staging schedule
governance.sharingPolicy: internal to the tenant and Kitry integration staff; endpoints and mappings shared with the customer's IT and the external provider under the integration agreement; never shared between tenants

assets.name: Implementation Project
assets.description: One customer deployment or major change run by Kitry's implementation and customer success consultants through the four phases (functional assessment, configuration, project management, training): scope and modules, countries and establishments, sites and user populations, workshop outputs and decisions, configuration backlog, data migration plan from the legacy system with mapping, test loads, defect list and sign-off, HRIS and SSO integration tasks, training sessions and attendance, change management actions, go-live readiness checklist, milestone dates against the contracted schedule, risks and issues, and the hand-over to support and account management. Managed in the Implementation, Migration and Training Workspace (impl) and linked to the tenant configuration, the HRIS import batches and the migration batches it produces.
assets.businessMeaning: Go-live on schedule and migration defect rate are the consultants' KPIs; the project object is where 35 years of deployment method become a repeatable plan.
assets.accessScope: Kitry implementation, migration, training and account management staff for their projects; the customer's project team for their own project status, decisions and checklists; medical content of migrated files never visible in the project

interfaces.name: implementation-project api
interfaces.description: Project, phase, workshop, backlog, migration plan, test load, defect, training session, readiness checklist, milestone and hand-over API used by the implementation workspace, configuration, HRIS import, support and account management.

interfaces.name: project deliverables
interfaces.description: Functional assessment reports, configuration specifications, migration mapping and sign-off documents, training materials and go-live reports.

interfaces.name: project events
interfaces.description: Phase started, workshop held, migration load completed, defect raised or closed, training delivered, go-live approved and handed over events consumed by configuration, support, account management and Kitry delivery dashboards.

governance.retention: kept for the life of the customer relationship plus 5 years; migration sign-off and defect records kept as evidence for the same period
governance.sharingPolicy: internal to Kitry and the customer's project team; delivery statistics aggregated across customers for Kitry's own steering; never customer-specific content across tenants

assets.name: Support Ticket
assets.description: A support request, incident or account interaction between a customer and Kitry: requester and role, tenant and module, category (question, incident, configuration change, regulatory question, data correction, integration failure, security), priority and service level, description and attachments with medical content forbidden by policy, diagnosis and resolution, the logged and time-limited access used to investigate, linked configuration changes and release items, satisfaction feedback, plus account management records (regulatory update communications, quarterly reviews, module and user growth, renewal and expansion opportunities). Managed in Support and Account Management (supp) by reactive support teams and the dedicated account managers assigned to each customer.
assets.businessMeaning: Support ticket resolution time is a consultant's KPI and the account record is where module and workforce growth per customer is won; the ticket is also the boundary that keeps Kitry staff out of medical content.
assets.accessScope: Kitry support, account management and, when escalated, engineering and regulatory content staff; the requester and the customer's tenant administrators for their own tickets; investigation access to tenant data logged and time-limited; medical content excluded

interfaces.name: support-ticket api
interfaces.description: Ticket creation from the application and portals, categorisation, service-level timer, investigation access request, resolution, linked change and account record API used by support, account management, configuration, notifications and Kitry delivery dashboards.

interfaces.name: ticket events
interfaces.description: Opened, prioritised, investigation access granted, resolved, reopened, closed and account review logged events consumed by notifications, configuration, the audit trail and Kitry service dashboards.

governance.retention: tickets kept 5 years after closure; investigation access records kept 10 years with the audit trail; account records for the life of the customer relationship plus 5 years
governance.sharingPolicy: internal to Kitry and the customer's requesters and administrators; service statistics reported to the customer in account reviews; never shared between tenants

stores.name: HDS Shared Tenant DB
stores.description: Multi-tenant PostgreSQL cluster on Kitry's HDS-certified (Hébergeur de Données de Santé) and ISO 27001-certified shared SaaS environment inside the EEA, with row-level tenant keys and a separate, physician-only medical schema per tenant for workers, organisations, exposures, surveillance schedules, appointments, consultations, fitness opinions, medical files, risk assessments, actions, chemicals, accidents, declarations, portal requests and the platform's identity, configuration and country regulation content schemas; encrypted at rest with per-tenant keys, no access from outside the EEA.

stores.name: HDS Dedicated Tenant DB
stores.description: Single-tenant PostgreSQL cluster provisioned for customers on the Dedicated HDS SaaS tier (large public bodies, transport operators, groups that require physical isolation or a named French HDS hosting region), running the same schemas, migrations and medical-schema segregation as the shared cluster with customer-specific backup windows, key custody and network peering; still operated exclusively inside the EEA under HDS and ISO 27001.

stores.name: Encrypted Medical Document Object Store
stores.description: Encrypted, versioned object storage on HDS-certified infrastructure for medical documents (fitness opinions and their signed PDFs, certificates, specialist reports, imaging and lab results attached to the file, vaccination certificates, questionnaire PDFs), safety data sheets and chemical labels, inspection and audit evidence photos, accident attachments and generated regulatory and annual reports; envelope encryption per tenant, immutable once signed or finalised, retention class attached to every object.

stores.name: Medical Device Measurement Store
stores.description: Store for raw and normalised outputs of connected measurement devices (Eolys, FIM, Essilor, JLM Medical, Siemens): audiograms, spirometry curves and flow-volume loops, vision test results, ECG traces, biometric readings and device calibration metadata, keyed by consultation and worker and retained alongside the medical file so trends can be compared across decades of surveillance; HDS-hosted, physician-scope access only.

stores.name: Prevention Analytics Warehouse
stores.description: Per-tenant analytical warehouse behind dashboards, KPIs, regulatory and annual reports and collective health monitoring, holding governed copies of workforce, exposure, surveillance, appointment, fitness-status, risk, action, chemical, accident and declaration facts with daily snapshots; medical content never lands here except as physician-approved aggregates that meet a minimum group-size threshold, and worker identifiers are pseudonymised at load.

stores.name: Notification and Message Store
stores.description: Queue and delivery log for convocation letters, SMS reminders (Cegedim gateway), e-mails, portal notifications and teleconsultation invitations, with template version, rendered content, channel, delivery and read status, opt-out and bounce handling; message bodies carry appointment logistics only and never medical content.

stores.name: Audit Log Store
stores.description: Append-only, tamper-evident store for every read and write of health data, access grants and break-glass openings of medical files, fitness-opinion releases to employers, declarations submitted to national bodies, configuration and role changes, exports, downloads and administrative events across all tenants, retained to satisfy HDS, ISO 27001 and medical-secrecy accountability and to answer worker access requests.

stores.name: Integration Staging Zone
stores.description: Secure, access-logged landing zone for HRIS extracts and API deltas (SAP SuccessFactors, Workday, ADP, national public-sector HR systems), legacy migration exports from previous occupational health software, device export files, e-signature envelopes and national-connector payloads and acknowledgements (Ameli, Fedris, insurers), held with checksums and validation results until accepted into the tenant database or rejected, then purged on a short schedule.

stores.name: Domain Event Bus
stores.description: Platform-wide, tenant-scoped event bus carrying workforce, exposure, surveillance, appointment, consultation, fitness-opinion, file, consent, risk, hazardous-situation, inspection, action, chemical, accident, declaration, portal, account, configuration and audit events to scheduling, notifications, portals, dashboards, the warehouse, integrations and the audit trail; medical events carry identifiers and state, never clinical content.
